newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Caller warns of 'bomb' at Japan's Jakarta embassy.
newsitem.headline: Caller warns of 'bomb' at Japan's Jakarta embassy.

text.p: Indonesian police searched the Japanese embassy in Jakarta on Wednesday after the second telephoned bomb threat to the mission in eight days.
An embassy official contacted by phone said staff had been cleared from the main building.
"Police with embassy staff are checking the building. Nothing has been found so far," the official said.
A policeman inside the embassy compound said an anonymous caller had phoned at 9:25 a.m. (0225 GMT) and said there was a bomb in the building. He then hung up the phone.

The embassy on one of the main throughfares through Jakarta's central business district was evacuated following a hoax telephoned bomb threat on Wednesday last week on the eve of Indonesia's general elections.
Diplomatic sources said they were unable to explain why the Japanese embassy was being targetted.

The main strain in relations between Indonesia and Japan at the moment is a complaint by Tokyo -- along with similar complaints from the United States and the European Union -- to the World Trade Organisation (WTO) over Jakarta's national car policy.

Indonesia has given tax and tariff breaks to a company headed by one of President Suharto's sons in conjunction with a South Korean firm to produce a national car, which Japan and other complainants say breaks WTO rules.
